53_marg3916: And he did not obtain the principality; but at the end his treacherous plots were overtaken by confusion, and as a fugitive he went again into the land of the Ammanites.
53_marg3917: At last, shut up to his own destruction by Aretas, tyrant of the Arabs, fleeing from city to city, hated by all, as a deserter of the laws and detestable as an enemy of his country and fellow citizens, he was thrust out into Egypt.
53_marg3918: And he that had driven many out of their country, perished in a strange land, going to Lacedemon. But when Menelaus, before Antiochus Eupator, was devising frauds in like manner as before, the King of kings stirred up the mind of Antiochus against the sinner; and upon Lysias suggesting that he was the cause of all the evils, he commanded (as the custom is with them) that he should be apprehended and put to death in the same place. Now in that very place there was a tower of fifty cubits, having on every side a heap of ashes. This had a steep prospect downward; thence the sacrilegious man was commanded to be cast into the ashes, all pushing him to destruction; and by such a law it befalls the transgressor of the law to die, and Menelaus not to be given to the earth. For because he had committed many sins against the altar of God, the fire and ashes of which were holy, he himself was condemned to die in ashes. Josephus relates, as we showed in the previous book, that the son of the chief priest Onias, when he was left a little boy after his father’s death, seeing that the king had killed his uncle Menelaus and had given the chief priesthood to Alchimus, who was not of the race of priests, but being turned by Lysias so as to transfer the honor from that family to another house, fled to Ptolemy king of Egypt, and merited honor from him and his wife Cleopatra, and asked a place in the region of Heliopolis, where he founded a city of his own name, having built a temple in the likeness of his father’s temple. But Alchimus, bearing enmity against Judas Machabeus, not long after was struck by the anger of God and perished; and so with the favor of all the Jews the priesthood was decreed to Judas Machabeus. All these things seem to build up a moral rather than an allegorical understanding, since they plainly show the most just judge and most equitable rewarder restoring to each a worthy recompense, as their deserts have required: that is, to the pious and God-fearing, eternal rewards; but to the impious and sinners and blasphemers, the punishment of everlasting fire. Nor ought anyone to flatter himself, on account of earthly happiness and the prosperity of the present life, that if he chooses to pass his life in sins he can escape as though unpunished; nor ought he who does well, and is hard pressed in the present life by severe torments or various tribulations, to despair of future salvation, if he perseveres in the path of justice, because it is written: “Many are the afflictions of the just; but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.” And: “Many are the scourges of the sinner, but mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord. Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye just, and glory, all ye right of heart.”
53_marg3919: After the writer of the History had told of the death of Lysimachus and Jason, impious and sacrilegious men, and had besides recounted the vision of signs and prodigies in the air, he returned to the order of the narrative, that is, to the departure of Antiochus Epiphanes from Egypt; who, irritated because by the command of the senate he was ordered to withdraw from the region of the Ptolemies which he had invaded, came to Judea with a furious mind, as was shown in the previous book, and took the city of Jerusalem by force of arms, and fined the people, plundered the temple, and committed many wicked deeds in it from the land. That Antiochus himself bears the figure of antichrist is most manifest from the tradition of the holy fathers. For as the Saviour has Solomon and the other saints as a type of his coming, so antichrist is rightly believed to have had the worst king Antiochus, who persecuted the saints and violated the temple, as a type of himself.
53_marg3920: And whereas he was set against, etc. The previous book also makes mention of this place, where both the slaying of the Jews in the quiet of the sabbath and the wickedness of Apollonius, together with his death, are told throughout Judea. But that Antiochus commanded Apollonius to kill all that were of perfect age and to sell the women and the younger sort signifies that their ancient enemy chiefly plans the death of those whom he has seen to be perfect in the Christian religion; but those who are soft and unstable, of whom it is written, “The fool is changed like the moon,” entangled in various errors, he scatters by winnowing them through divers vices, separates them from the land of the Church, and casts them far into the depth of crimes.
53_marg3921: But how he says that Judas Machabeus was the tenth I do not find, unless perhaps by the enumeration of the high priests who were in the Jewish nation in the times of the kingdom of the Greeks. In the times of Seleucus Nicanor, from whom the history of the kingdom of the Greeks reckons the years, the first high priest was Onias the son of Jaddus; the second Simeon the son of Onias; the third Eleazar the brother of Simon; the fourth Manasses, uncle of Eleazar; the fifth Onias the son of Simon the Just; the sixth Simon the son of Onias; the seventh Onias the son of Simon; the eighth another Onias, who was called Jason, brother of the former Onias; the ninth Menelaus, brother of Jason; the tenth Judas, who, when Alchimus was attempting to seize the high priesthood of the Jews and was destroyed by divine judgment, received with the wonderful consent of all the dignity of the first priesthood. Spiritually, however, Judas is deservedly called the tenth, because he is found to have kept the precepts of the Decalogue perfectly in faith and devotion, and, zealous for the law itself, to have been the first after his father to defend it with arms from the hands of enemies. He is well written to have led his life among wild beasts with his company in the mountains and to have eaten food of hay, because, following the examples of the saints, for they are the mountains of God, despising the bestial ways of persecutors, he chose a life pleasing to God, and thought it best to feed himself on the ever-green pasture of the virtues, so that, nourished by the unfailing food of the soul, he might not feel everlasting hunger. But the reading of the acts of Judas profits us only if we are willing to imitate the virtues of his constancy and sobriety, and do not set the delights of the world and the pomp of this age before the justice and truth of God, ever mindful of that saying of the Lord which says: “For what doth it profit a man, if he gain the whole world, and suffer the loss of his own soul?” And again: “He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world, keepeth it unto life eternal.”
53_marg3922: These same things are related in the earlier book: that Antiochus through his envoys defiled the temple, building an idol of desolation upon the altar of God, of which place we have set down the allegory there; nor did anyone openly confess himself to be a Jew.
53_marg3923: The Gentiles said that Liber Pater was the god of wine, whose rites Antiochus ordered to be celebrated especially on his birthday, because he believed that this god favoured his birthday. For he wished Liber to be named from “liberation,” because males in coupling are, as it were, set free by his benefit, their seed being emitted. For which reason Liber is there painted with a womanly and delicate body. For they say that women were assigned to him, and wine, for the arousing of lust. Whence also his brow is girded with a vine garland. But he has a crown of vine and a horn for this reason, that when wine is drunk gratefully and moderately it affords gladness, but when it rouses beyond measure it stirs up strifes, that is, as it were gives horns. The same is also called Lyeus, from the drink of Lyeus, because the limbs are loosened by much wine. He is also called in Greek Nisius, from Niso, a mountain of India, where he is said to have been nursed; moreover there is also a city Nisa, in which the same Liber is worshipped. Whence he was called Niseus. Orpheus first brought the rites of Liber Pater into Greece, and first celebrated them on a mountain of Boeotia, and at Thebes, where Liber was born, the mountain nearest; which, since it often resounded with the song of the cithara, was called Cithaeron; and the rites are even now called Orphic, in which he himself was afterwards torn to pieces, and taken. And he lived at almost the same times as Faunus, but which of them was earlier in age can be doubted. For in the same years Latinus and Priam reigned. Likewise their fathers Picus and Laomedon, in whose reign Orpheus came with the Argonauts to the shore of the Athenians.
53_marg3924: Then Eleazar, etc. This Eleazar, whom the impiety of the most cruel king Antiochus compelled in his old age to eat swine’s flesh, signifies the Christian people, whom the cruelty of antichrist near the end of the world will strive to turn to idolatry and the filth of life. Now Eleazar means “my God, helper,” a name that fits most aptly the people of the faithful. Who know how to say with the Psalmist to the Lord: “Thou art my helper, O God, forsake me not.” And again: “My deliverer, my God, in him will I trust.” But as the savagery of the most wicked king could not compel Eleazar to eat swine’s flesh, so neither will the cruelty of antichrist be able in any way to defile the company of the elect with any uncleanness.
53_marg3925: What is signified by this mother of seven sons, if not the fruitfulness of mother Church, who by the grace of the sevenfold spirit begets sons adopted to God the Father? Though the cruelty of the typical Antiochus, that is, of antichrist, tears them together with their mother with various torments, partly by his ministers, partly by himself, yet he is in no way able to drag them to blasphemy. And what reward awaits this woman and her sons in the future for the labour which they have endured in the present, Isaias shows, saying: “Give praise, O thou barren, that bearest not: sing forth praise, and make a joyful noise, thou that didst not travail with child: for many are the children of the desolate, more than of her that hath a husband, saith the Lord. Enlarge the place of thy tent, and stretch out the skins of thy tabernacles, spare not: lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes. For thou shalt pass on to the right hand and to the left, and thy seed shall inherit the Gentiles. Fear not, for thou shalt not be confounded, nor blush: for thou shalt not be put to shame, because thou shalt forget the shame of thy youth, and shalt remember no more the reproach of thy widowhood, because he that made thee shall be condemned of thee [sic: the Latin reads “damnabitur tui qui fecit te Dominus”; render as: for he that made thee, the Lord, shall be named], and thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, shall be called the God of all the earth. For the Lord hath called thee as a woman forsaken and mourning in spirit, and as a wife cast off from her youth, said thy God. For a moment in a little time have I forsaken thee, but with great mercies will I gather thee. In a moment of indignation have I hid my face a little while from thee, but with everlasting kindness have I had mercy on thee, said the Lord thy Redeemer. Thou poor little one, tossed with tempest, without all comfort: behold I will lay thy stones in order, and will found thee in sapphires, and I will make thy bulwarks of jasper: and thy gates of graven stones, and all thy borders of desirable stones. All thy children shall be taught of the Lord: and great shall be the peace of thy children. And thou shalt be founded in justice: depart far from oppression.” And that last of all, after the sons, the mother also was consumed, shows that after the triumphs of the individual sons of the Church, by which, conquering their enemies, they will enter as free souls into eternal rest, last of all the mother herself of all the faithful will be consummated at the end of the world, and, taking the trophy of glory over all her enemies, will possess an everlasting kingdom. But how the most blessed martyr and sweetest teacher Cyprian, writing to Fortunatus about these same seven brothers, discoursed in eloquent speech after the manner of rhetors, we have judged should be inserted in this place; among other things he says thus: What do the seven brothers in the Machabees, perhaps alike in birth and in virtues, signify, if not the number seven, filled with the mystery of perfect consummation? For as the seven brothers were joined together in martyrdom, as first in the divine ordering there were seven days, containing seven thousand years, as the seven spirits, as the seven angels, who stand and attend before the face of God, and the sevenfold lamp in the tabernacle of the testimony, and in the Apocalypse the seven golden candlesticks, and in Solomon the seven pillars, upon which wisdom builds a house, so also this number of seven brothers embraces the seven Churches by the amount of its number, according as we read in the first book of Kings that the barren woman bore seven, and in Isaias seven women take hold of one man, begging that his name be called upon them. And the apostle Paul, who remembers this lawful and fixed number, writes to seven Churches. And in the Apocalypse the Lord directs his divine commands and heavenly precepts to seven Churches and to their angels. He is now found here, now among the brothers, that the lawful consummation may be completed; she is plainly joined with seven children, and the mother, the origin and root, who afterwards bore seven Churches, is herself the first and one, founded upon the rock by the voice of the Lord. Nor is it without meaning that in the passions the mother alone is with her children. For the martyrs, who in their passion testify that they are sons of God, are now reckoned only as having God for Father, as the Lord teaches in the Gospel, saying: “Call none your father upon earth; for one is your father, who is in heaven.” What proclamations of confession they uttered, how splendid, what great proofs of faith they gave! King Antiochus, hostile, or rather antichrist expressed in Antiochus, sought to defile with the contagion of the flesh the glorious mouths of the martyrs, unconquered by the spirit of confession; and when he had gravely beaten them with scourges and could accomplish nothing, he ordered frying pans to be heated. When they were heated and kindled, he commanded that the one who had spoken first, and who by the constancy of his courage and faith had the more provoked the king’s anger, be brought forward and fried, the tongue, which had confessed the Lord, having first been drawn out and pulled forth. What a glorious thing befell the martyr! For the tongue that confessed the name of the Lord ought itself to go first to the Lord. Afterwards, in the second, having devised sharper punishments, before he tortured the other members he tore off the skin of the head with the hair, from hatred, evidently a sure one. For since the head of man is Christ, and the head of Christ is God, he who tore the head in the martyr of the Lord was persecuting Christ in the head.
53_marg3926: But he, in his martyrdom, promising himself also the reward of the resurrection from God’s recompense, cried out and said: “Thou indeed, powerless one, destroyest us out of this present life, but the King of the world will raise us up, who die for his laws, in the resurrection of eternal life.” The third, when his tongue was demanded, quickly put it forth. For having already learned from his brother to despise the punishment of the tongue to be cut out, he also steadfastly showed his hands to be cut off. Greatly blessed in this kind of punishment, to whom it befell, with hands stretched out to the torment, to imitate the likeness of the Lord’s passion.
53_marg3927: Likewise the fourth also, despising the torments with equal courage, answering with a heavenly voice to rebuke the king, cried out and said: It is better, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God, to be raised up again by him; for as to thee, thou shalt have no resurrection unto life.
53_marg3928: The fifth, on account of the executioner’s rage, trampled the hard and various torments underfoot by the strength of his faith; and, armed or enlivened by the spirit of divinity also with foreknowledge and knowledge of things to come, he prophesied to the king the indignation of God and the vengeance that would swiftly follow. “Whereas thou hast power among men,” he says, “though thou art corruptible, thou dost what thou wilt.” Think not therefore that our nation is forsaken by God; “stay patiently a while, and thou shalt see his great power, in what manner he will torment thee and thy seed.” What a veil of martyrdom that was, how great, how mighty a comfort in his sufferings, not to think of his own torments but to proclaim the punishments of his tormentor. In the sixth, however, not virtue alone but humility also is to be proclaimed: that the martyr claimed nothing for himself, and did not toss about the honour of his confession in proud words, but rather ascribed it to his sins that he suffered persecution from the king, and gave to God that he would afterwards be avenged. He taught that martyrs are modest, trusting in vengeance and boasting of nothing in their passion.
53_marg3929: “Be not deceived without cause,” he says, “for we suffer these things for ourselves, having sinned against your God; but do not think that you will go unpunished, having undertaken to fight against God.” Admirable also was the mother, who, not broken by the weakness of her sex, nor moved by the manifold bereavement, looked willingly upon her dying children, and reckoned those punishments of her dear ones not as penalties but as glories, offering to God so great a martyrdom by the courage of her eyes, as her sons offered by the torments and the suffering of their limbs. When, six having been killed and punished, one of the brothers remained, to whom the king promised riches and power and many things, that his cruelty and fierceness might be soothed by the comfort of even one subdued, he also asked her to entreat her son along with him to cast him down. And the mother did entreat her son, but as became a mother of martyrs, as became one mindful of the law and of God, as became one loving her sons not softly but bravely. For she entreated him to confess the Lord; she entreated that the brother might not be separated from his brothers in the fellowship of praise and glory.
53_marg3930: Then, reckoning herself the mother of seven sons, it would befall her to have borne seven sons for God rather than for the world. Arming him therefore and strengthening him, and begetting her son by a happier birth: “My son,” she said, “have pity upon me, that bore thee nine months in my womb, and gave thee suck three years, and brought thee up unto this age,”
53_marg3931: I beseech thee, my son, look upon heaven and earth, and all that is in them: and consider that God made them out of nothing, and mankind also.
53_marg3932: and so let it be, that thou fear not this tormentor, but, being made worthy of thy brethren, mayest receive death, that in that mercy I may receive thee again with thy brethren. Great is the mother’s praise in exhorting to virtue, but greater in the fear of God and in the truth of faith, because she allowed nothing for herself or her son in the honour of the six martyrs, nor believed that the prayer of brothers would profit one denying unto salvation; she persuaded him rather to become a partaker of the passion, that on the day of judgment he might be found with his brothers. After this the mother also dies together with her children, nor was anything else now permitted than that she who had borne and made martyrs should be joined with them in the fellowship of glory, and that she should herself follow those whom she had sent ahead to God.
53_marg3933: But Judas Machabeus, etc. What the history of the former book relates concerning Mathathias, the father of Machabeus, and his brothers, the writer of the present book, striving for brevity, omits, and turns to narrate the deed and battles of Judas, relating some things of them but, in his manner, omitting very many. But since we have already expounded his allegory for the most part above, we do not think it necessary to repeat what has once been said. But if anyone asks what the six thousand men who were joined to Judas in the beginning signify, let him know that through the perfection of the number six and of the thousand, the perfect devotion of Christ’s soldiers in faith and sincerity is designated. Whence in the Acts of the Apostles it is written of the primitive Church among the Jews: “And the multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul: neither did any one say that aught of the things which he possessed, was his own; but all things were common unto them. And with great power did the apostles give testimony of the resurrection of Jesus Christ our Lord; and great grace was in them all.”
53_marg3934: But Philip, seeing, etc. In the former book it is written that Antiochus, about to set out for Persia, left Lysias within the kingdom, a nobleman of the blood royal, over the king’s affairs, and to bring up Antiochus his son; and that this Lysias chose Ptolemee the son of Dorymenus, and Nicanor, and Gorgias, mighty men of the king’s friends, and sent them with forty thousand men to destroy the Jews according to the king’s word. But now it is related here that Philip wrote to Ptolemee the governor to send aid to the king’s affairs, and that Ptolemee himself sent Nicanor for this, twenty thousand armed men being given him, Gorgias also, a military man, being joined to him. For this Philip the said king Antiochus, returning from Persia to Babylon, set over his whole kingdom, and gave him the crown, and his robe, and his ring, that he should bring up his son Antiochus, and nourish him, and he should reign. Him the aforesaid Lysias, returning to Antioch together with the younger Antiochus, and finding him ruling the city, overcame. Whence it is asked how Philip is said to order, through Ptolemee, the passage of Nicanor and Gorgias to Judea, when the former history relates that, while the elder Antiochus was staying in Persia, this same Gorgias the leader, together with Lysias his commander, were overcome and put to flight by the Jews, and that this was made known to Antiochus on his return, and that on this account he fell into sickness from sorrow, because it had not turned out with the Jews as he had planned. This, unless I am mistaken, is resolved in no other way than that Philip, the government being entrusted to him, wrote back that the governors of Syria should do this same thing which Lysias had before undertaken to do by his endeavour, but did not accomplish, nor even could he, as he himself had arranged, bring it about against the Jews by his own sending, as the following history shows.
53_marg3935: This was briefly recorded in the former book, namely that merchants came with gold and silver to buy the children of Israel as slaves for themselves. Here, however, it is told more clearly that by Nicanor, who promised the king to make up from the slaves taken from the Jews the tribute to be given to the Romans, the merchants themselves were invited to the purchase of the Jewish slaves.
53_marg3936: The former book does not say plainly of this coming of Nicanor into Judea, which took place under Antiochus; yet, relating that he was chosen through Lysias together with Ptolemee and Gorgias, powerful men, with a crowd of companions joined to them, to invade and lay waste Judea, it asserts that under Demetrius he was sent thither, and wished by guile to take Judas and invade Judea, but did not prevail. That Nicanor himself bears the type of hypocrites, who do all things feignedly, has been said above. But Judas, with seven thousand, fights against Nicanor and his companions, and conquers, because through the sevenfold grace of the Spirit the people of the Church, with its rulers, conquers all enemies, and neither Jew, nor pagan, nor heretic, nor schismatic, nor any hypocrite or wicked man ever takes victory from it. Rather, it shall possess with its conquering king the trophy of glory for ever.
53_marg3937: And when they kept the feast of the victory. For “epinichia” I read in another edition “days of victory.” The enemies being overcome, therefore, Judas celebrates a feast, because when any holy man triumphs over the ancient enemy through the grace of Christ, filled with spiritual joy, he ought to sing worthy praises and render manifold thanks to his author; nor is it fitting that he be ungrateful who has felt that he was helped by divine work.
53_marg3938: At that time. What was briefly noted in the former book about the end of Antiochus is explained more fully in this. Mystically, however, it shows that the persecutors of Christians, for their evil deeds and the works of injustice which they had done, will receive in the future a just retribution of punishments from the Lord; and those who here did not fear to trouble the hearts of the faithful will in the last vengeance be tormented by inward pains with late repentance, of which it is written in the book of Wisdom: “Then shall the just stand with great constancy against those that have afflicted them, and taken away their labours. These seeing it, shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the suddenness of their unexpected salvation, saying within themselves, repenting, and groaning for anguish of spirit: These are they whom we had sometime in derision, and for a parable of reproach. We fools esteemed their life madness, and their end without honour. Behold how they are numbered among the children of God, and their lot is among the saints. Therefore we have erred from the way of truth, and the light of justice hath not shined unto us, and the sun of understanding hath not risen upon us. We wearied ourselves in the way of iniquity and destruction, and have walked through hard ways, but the way of the Lord we have not known. What hath pride profited us? or what advantage hath the boasting of riches brought us? All those things are passed away like a shadow.”
53_marg3939: But upon the same day. This feast, which is read to have been celebrated in like manner on the twenty-fifth day of the month Casleu, which among the Latins is called December, is also recorded in the former book. But that it relates that they had earlier kept the feast of tabernacles in the mountains and in caves, wherefore they bore thyrsi and green branches and palms to him who prospered in cleansing his place, shows that in the present life, where is the place of tribulation and sorrow, we ought to acknowledge ourselves pilgrims, and that there we should strive to offer to God the Father the flowers of virtues and the ever-green branches of good works, for the obtaining of eternal life and the reward of heavenly recompense. For a thyrsus is generally the middle stalk of all herbs or pot-herbs, so called because it rises up from the earth. So too from our earth a useful shoot of matter ought to rise, that we may always render acceptable fruit to the tiller of our heart, who tends us by the gift of his Spirit.
53_marg3940: And of Antiochus indeed, etc. The history of the former book tells that Antiochus the noble, about to set out for Persia, appointed Lysias over the affairs of the kingdom, from the river Euphrates to the river of Egypt, and that he should bring up Antiochus his son until he should return. But now it is told that the same Antiochus, son of the noble Antiochus, that is, Eupator, appointed the same Lysias over the affairs of the kingdom. But because he says that he has abridged the account of the evils that were done in the wars, he shows that he has passed over in the order of the history those wars which Antiochus the Younger waged in person against the Jews, when he came there with elephants and a great multitude gathered from his own and other nations, and when Eleazar, son of Saura, killed the greatest of the elephants, supposing that the king was on it.
53_marg3941: This Gorgias, as we have already shown above, the former book relates that Lysias chose together with Ptolemee and Nicanor to attack Judea; how he fared in the attack is related in the former and in the present book. But it is declared that the victory fell to the Jews. For that this Gorgias, who provoked various nations to fight against the Jews, bears the type of the devil has already been said above; he incites unbelievers against the Church of Christ and stirs up war against its faithful. But because it is written there that Gorgias chose five thousand men for the battle, and also, by the multiplication of the number five in itself, twenty-five thousand are reported slain, it signifies that all who serve the devil with the five senses of the body through carnal desires are put to death in a fitting manner.
53_marg3942: But some, the spiritual Machabee fighting, the enemies being driven, flee into two towers, since those who strove to overthrow the faith of Christ, although in no way able to resist the truth of the Gospel, yet not believing unto salvation, through ignorance and not fearing the future judgment of the Lord, choose rather to flee into the towers of pride and idolatry than, pricked by the sorrows of penance, to forsake their errors; against whom Judas sends soldiers with Simon and Joseph; but some of them, held back by love of money, neglected to carry through the war committed to them, because it often happens that those to whom the priestly dignity and the warfare of the spiritual contest are committed, deceived by earthly covetousness, would rather satisfy their avarice than, despising earthly advantages, fulfil the will of Christ by fighting lawfully. But such men will not escape deserved punishments; rather, when the true teachers, strengthened by the Spirit of God, have destroyed the enemies by fighting and overcoming them, they themselves will be justly punished by them with the vengeance of anathema.
53_marg3943: This Timotheus holds the type of heretics, as we showed in the preceding book, who, both by themselves and also by the aid of others, always strive to destroy the faith of Christ and the truth of the Gospel; but against the wickedness of these, the holy doctors seek help from the Lord, and trusting with sure hope in the heavenly aid, they fight bravely against the enemies. The five horsemen who appeared on horses, adorned with golden bridles, and who gave leadership to the Jews, signify the five books of the law; when these have been brought back to spiritual knowledge, and the letter has been drawn from its figurative veil to the sense of the Gospel by spiritual knowledge, they furnish timely comfort to their followers, and, guarding the true confessors of Christ on the right and on the left by the two commandments of charity, they hurl at their adversaries the fiery darts of their sayings, and by these, confounded by blindness of mind and filled with disturbance of sense, they fall. Of these, twenty thousand and five hundred are laid low, when all who savour what is contrary to the catholic doctrine, which is in the two testaments, and to the grace of the Holy Spirit, are overcome and cast down, the truth conquering; likewise six hundred horsemen are crushed, when the pride of their mind, which hoped to prevail over the catholics, is utterly destroyed by the nod from on high.
53_marg3944: What is it that Timotheus, overcome by Judas, fleeing with his men into the fortified stronghold of Gazara, and trusting in the strength of the place, hurled curses from there at the people, but that heretics, divided and separated from the unity of the right faith, committing themselves to the hiding-places of their errors, and trusting in the defence of their cunning, hurl words of cursing against the catholics? For Timotheus is interpreted beneficent, or rather poisoner, and Gazara, division or cutting off. But Judas with his companions, besieging the stronghold for four days, at last through twenty young men with spirits inflamed on account of the blasphemy broke into the fortification, set fire to the towers and gates, and burned alive the very cursers; so the holy doctors, shutting in the enemies on every side with the four books of the Gospel, through those who keep the commands of the law by the two commandments of charity destroy their devices, and burn them alive with the fire of sorrow and penance; and thus, in two days, laying waste with the two testaments the stronghold of all errors, they slay with the sword of the word of God the true Timotheus, that is, the devil, the head of all error and author of all evil, who wishes to lie hid in his wickedness.
53_marg3945: And a short time after, Lysias, etc. In the earlier book of this history it is written that Lysias, when the business of the kingdom was committed to him by Antiochus, who was surnamed Epiphanes, that is, illustrious, fought against the Jews, where, battle being joined, there fell in the army of Lysias five thousand men; and Lysias, seeing the flight of his own men and the boldness of the Jews, went away to Antioch, to gather together again the forces of his army, intending to go again into Judea. But now, because it is related that again under Antiochus Eupator he came into Judea, and there, having waged the war unhappily, fled and escaped shamefully, it appears that the same Lysias fought against the Jews under both kings Antiochus, that is, father and son, and in each battle was beaten by the Jews; but at last, compelled by his own confusion and terrified by the inroad of Philip into the kingdom, as has been shown elsewhere, he persuaded the king to make peace with the Hebrews, which nevertheless he did not keep.
53_marg3946: Bethsura was a city in the tribe of Juda or Benjamin, and to this day Bethsura is a village, as we go from Elia to Hebron, near the twentieth milestone, by which a spring, bubbling up at the foot of the mountain, is swallowed up by the same ground in which it is born; and the Acts of the Apostles report that the eunuch of Candace the queen was baptized by Philip in this place.
53_marg3947: But when Machabeus, etc. What Lysias, the cruellest enemy of the Jews, signifies, who holds the rule of the pagans and who harass the Church of God with most grievous persecutions, has already been said. When he persecutes the confessors of Christ with most grievous scandals, and, leaning on the standing of his pride, is lifted up by the empty favour of his followers, he plots in his heart to profane the sanctuary and trample on the law of God. But in his deeds he does not prosper according to the fraud he planned, but rather is put to flight and laid low by the soldiers of Christ, who seek help from on high with most humble prayers. To them a leader, a horseman in white garment and golden arms, is sent, because to them is granted the most pure incarnation of God and men, for crushing the obstinacy of all enemies, whose golden arms, that is, his sayings and examples, are most glorious and precious, nor is there power in heaven, nor on earth, nor under the earth, that can resist him. But as was foreshown in the prophetic vision in Daniel, the stone cut out of the mountain without hands broke in pieces the gold, the silver, the brass, the iron, and it is a holy great mountain, which fills the whole earth, whose kingdom shall never be destroyed, and his kingdom shall not be delivered up to another people, and it shall break in pieces and consume all the kingdoms, and itself shall stand for ever. But the saints of the most high God shall take the kingdom, and they shall possess it for ever and ever.
53_marg3948: In the year one hundred and forty-eight, of Dioscorus. That month, which among the Greeks is called Dioscorus, is the same that among the Latins is called June; to this month, therefore, the sign of the Gemini is ascribed. Whence the poet says: “June sees the Laconians go equal in the heaven.” For the Gemini, that is, Castor and Pollux, are called in Greek Dioscori. Of this matter the city of the Colchians is a witness, which, built by Amphius and Circius, the charioteers of the twins, was named Dioscori after their name. For many interpret dioscori as charioteers. But the Gemini are, as we have said, Castors. But that Lysias, compelled by fear of the Jews, persuaded Antiochus to enter into a covenant with the Jews, shows that the enemies of the Church are often overcome by divine power, and yield to her, though not from will yet from necessity, when they cannot bring to effect what they wish.
53_marg3949: But in the hundredth year, etc. The month Xanthicus among the Athenians is the one which among us is called April, and among the Hebrews Nisan, among whom, according to the precept of the law, this same month is the first of the months of the year, in which they also celebrate the Passover.
53_marg3950: The men of Joppe, etc. These men of Joppe, of whom the Scripture tells, were inhabitants of a town of Palestine, which is called Joppe, a seaport situated in the tribe of Dan; and, to touch briefly on something from the fables of the Gentiles, lofty rocks are shown there to this day, set on the shore of the sea, on which Andromeda, banished there, is said to have been delivered by the help of Perseus, her one-time husband. But according to the mystical sense, these same men of Joppe, who dwelling by the sea had given scandal to the Jews, signify heretics, dwelling near the waves of the turbulent world, who always lie in wait for the Jews, that is, for the true confessors of Christ, and strive to draw into the pit of their errors whomsoever they can of their number. So the men of Joppe, as it were, set up boats, in which they plunge into the deep the Jews led away from the shore, when heretics, forging wicked doctrines, adorn them with fair speech, which the name of the men of Joppe can well signify; for it is interpreted beauty; so that they may more easily, by the glibness of their tongue, draw simple people away from the right faith, gather them to themselves, and cast the unwary headlong into the abyss of perdition. But the typical Judas does not allow this to go far; rather, finding the murderers lurking in the darkness of their error, he torments them with the vengeance of just retribution, and, showing that their frauds are owed to the everlasting fire, he rightly strikes them, together with the authors of the wickedness themselves, with the sword of anathema, and does not allow the poison of their malice to lie hidden any longer.
53_marg3951: But when he understood, etc. By Jamnia, which is interpreted sea, can be understood the assembly of schismatics, who are always in a tempest. Schism, then, as some hold, is so called from a rending of minds. For one believes with the same worship and the same rite as the rest, and delights only in the division of the congregation; and schism is made when they say: We sanctify the unclean, and other like things. Judas learns that the men of Jamnia are doing in like manner, as the men of Joppe plotted snares for the Jews dwelling with them, when the holy doctors, finding the guile of the schismatics like the fraud of the heretics, fear deception from them for the faithful, against whom they stir up war, and finding them in the darkness of superstition, burn them together with their devices by the fire of excommunication; so that their burning appears at Jerusalem, that is, so that the condemnation of their error may be made manifest to all the worshippers of the true religion. Whence also Paul writes to Timothy, and in making manifest the errors of the foolish says: “But know this, that in the last days shall come on dangerous times. Men shall be lovers of themselves, covetous, haughty, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, wicked, without affection, without peace, slanderers, incontinent, unmerciful, without kindness; traitors, stubborn, puffed up, lovers of pleasures more than of God; having an appearance indeed of godliness, but denying the power thereof. Now these avoid. For of these sort are they who creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, who are led away with divers desires: ever learning, and never attaining to the knowledge of the truth. Now as Jannes and Mambres resisted Moses, so these also resist the truth, men corrupted in mind, reprobate concerning the faith. But they shall proceed no farther; for their folly shall be manifest to all men, as theirs also was.” Likewise the prince of the apostles, stirring the faithful to guard against the guile of wicked men, says: “You therefore, brethren, knowing these things before, take heed lest, being led aside by the error of the unwise, you fall from your own steadfastness. But grow in grace and in the knowledge of our Lord, to him be glory both now and in the day of eternity. Amen.”
53_marg3952: And when they were now gone from thence, etc. The Arabians, who are interpreted humble, or western, can signify those who love worldly and secular wisdom, which is deservedly called humble and western, because it does not know how to imitate the true wisdom that comes from heaven. Intent on this, therefore, they fight against Judas and his companions with five thousand men and five hundred horsemen, because, entangled in the senses and pursuits of the flesh, everything of the spiritual sense that is brought to them by the holy doctors seems to them, as it were, contrary and profane. Whence they also strive to rebel against them; but, overcome as the truth grows bright and overpowered by the constancy of the holy preachers, they ask that right hands be given them, so that, forsaking their errors, they seek the unity of the catholic faith and desire to join themselves to the confessors of Christ. To these the spiritual Judas, seeing that in many things they can become useful, promises peace, gives right hands, and allows them to depart unharmed; because often such men, who had been steeped in the philosophy of the world, when they are converted to the faith of Christ, become fitter and more able for destroying the foolishness and error of the Gentiles, and when the word of faith has been fully preached to them, equipped with both kinds of armour they fight more strongly against unbelief. Hence Solomon, in building the temple, asks help of Hiram, king of Tyre, for cutting timber from Libanus, because the servants of Hiram were more skilled in this art than his own servants; but they did not press on at this work by themselves alone, rather, joined with the servants of Solomon, they carried it out vigorously and fittingly; the figure of which matter is plain, because the apostles surely knew more surely the word of the Gospel, which they had heard from the Lord. But the Gentiles, converted from error and to the truth of the Gospel through the same apostles, learned to overcome and empty them more skilfully.
53_marg3953: He laid siege, etc. This city, under whose fortification very many crowds of different nations gathered and dwelt, I judge to signify nothing better than the power of this world, under whose dominion different nations came, that under their defence they might be protected in body and enjoy the pleasure of their flesh. Such an assembly, therefore, trusting in the firmness of the walls, provoked Juda with curses, and blaspheming spoke what it was not lawful to speak, when various persons, favouring the flattery of princes and rejoicing in their benefits, acted against the holy preachers, and praising idols hurled words of blasphemy against the divinity itself. Judas therefore, having called upon the prince of the world, took the city by his help, because the holy doctors fought against their adversaries, partly by prayers, partly by doctrines, until by the word of God, through the will of the Lord, they captured the princes themselves; and so they wrought unspeakable slaughters of men, not that they should perish utterly by eternal destruction, but that, dying to the world, they might live more happily in Christ. Such slaughters also it is right for Peter to work in the Acts of the Apostles, when in ecstasy he had seen that mystical vessel let down from heaven to earth by four beginnings, in which were all the fourfooted beasts and creeping things of the earth and fowls of the air, and it was said to him: “Arise, Peter, kill and eat.” Those animals, therefore, signified all nations unclean by errors, but to be cleansed in the name of the holy Trinity by sacred baptism, who, leaving the image of man, took on the shapes of beasts and serpents by imitation; and the heavenly voice bids Peter kill and eat them, who commanded him to kill in the Gentiles what they had been, and to make them what he himself was. For he who eats food laid outside passes it into his own body. He commanded, therefore, that the nations, laid before the doors through unbelief, their past life being slain, be joined to the Church, which Peter signifies, according to what the apostle Paul says of himself: “For I through the law am dead to the law, that I may live to God,” and again: “And I live, now not I; but Christ liveth in me.” Nor is this without mystery, that the adjoining pool seemed to flow with blood because of the slaughter of men wrought; because the shedding of blood signifies the loss of a bloody life, as though the water seems to flow stained with blood, when in the sacrament of baptism, where the faithful die to sin, bloody works and the filth of carnal life are known to be washed away, when “the old man is put off with his deeds, and the new is put on, who according to God is created in justice and holiness of truth.”
53_marg3954: And they came to Caratha, etc. I have heard a certain Hebrew explaining that those Jews are called Tubianites, who, summoned from foreigners, came to help Judas, and were called Tubianites as if hired with foreign trumpets.
53_marg3955: These two captains, that is, Dositheus and Sosipater, designate the holy preachers, who by the disposition of the true Machabeus, that is, of the most valiant warrior, of whom it is written in the Psalm, “The Lord strong and mighty, mighty in battle,” are appointed to wage war against all the errors of the faithless; and they are fittingly marked by the number two, because, well instructed by the spiritual knowledge of the two testaments, they are known to accomplish the battle of the Lord rightly. These therefore slay ten thousand men left by Timotheus in the hold, when, by the authority of the same law, and by the spiritual sword, they justly slay the associates of heresiarchs, set up by them to defend their wickedness, who think things contrary to the law of God, and themselves the truth.
53_marg3956: But Judas was vehemently, etc. The question is asked how Timotheus is here said to have been let go alive by the captains of Judas, because of the humility of his prayers, since he had the parents and brethren of many of the Jews, who would happen to be deceived by his death if he were killed; and a little before it is told that he had been slain in the hold of Gazara by the soldiers of Judas. For if he had been killed there then, he could in no way have been let go alive here. This, unless I am mistaken, can be resolved in no other way than that either he is said to be slain there by anticipation, or that the Timotheus who was killed in the hold of Gazara is understood to be one, and this one, who is read to have been let go through Dositheus and Sosipater, another. But that the captains of Judas, considering the advantage of their brethren and the redemption of their own, spared Timotheus, shows that sometimes errant men are to be dealt with more gently; I do not say that their iniquity should be consented to, but that their weakness be provided for with fatherly piety, and especially in those places where some fruit is hoped for from the conversion of the erring, so that by ecclesiastical gentleness they may be moved to escape the snares of the devil and come to catholic liberty. Whence in the African council it was decreed concerning the Donatist heretics that they should be dealt with more lightly, where it is thus written: When all things that seemed to suit the advantage of the Church had been discussed and considered, with the Spirit of God consenting and admonishing, we have chosen to deal gently and peacefully with the aforesaid men, although cut off by restless dissension from the unity of the Lord’s body, so that, as far as lies in us, it may be made fully known throughout all the African provinces to all who are entangled in their communion and fellowship, with how wretched an error they are overcome; lest perhaps, as the Apostle says, when we correct in meekness those who are of a different mind, “God may give them repentance to know the truth, and they may recover themselves from the snares of the devil, by whom they are held captive at his will.”
53_marg3957: We said in the exposition of the former book, where Timothy was treated, that his army signified the crowd of heretics; likewise of the inhabitants of the city Ephron, that they figuratively expressed those who thought they should follow the rite of Judaism in the times of grace, such as were the Jews themselves and the Ebionite heretics and the rest who wished to keep the ceremonies of the law with the Gospel. But because these, thinking carnally, were unwilling to learn spiritual knowledge, and could not understand that “the end of the law is Christ, unto justice to every one that believeth,” that is, Jew and Gentile, therefore five thousand are read to have been laid low in the Ephronite war, as in that war which was fought at Carmon, because “the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God,” and “the wisdom of the flesh is death.” For “the letter killeth, but the spirit quickeneth.” Whence the same is said through Paul: “God hath made foolish the wisdom of this world.” And again: “The sensual man perceiveth not these things that are of the Spirit of God; for it is foolishness to him, and he cannot understand, because it is spiritually examined.” Hence James the apostle, writing to the dispersed, says: “But if you have bitter zeal, and there be contentions in your hearts; glory not, and be not liars against the truth. For this is not wisdom descending from above, from the Father of lights, but earthly, sensual, devilish.” Its followers, the princes of the peoples, he calls “fountains without water, and clouds tossed with whirlwinds, to whom the mist of darkness is reserved.” For they are speakers of vanities, who “allure by the desires of fleshly riotousness those who for a little while escape, such as converse in error, promising them liberty, whereas they themselves are the slaves of corruption.” For Judas with his men everywhere laid low the crowds of enemies and won the victory, because the holy teachers, asserters of the truth and conquerors of every error, helped by divine aid, everywhere take from their enemies the trophy of victory, whence they can say with Paul: “Now thanks be to God, who always maketh us to triumph in Christ Jesus, and manifesteth the odour of his knowledge by us in every place.”
53_marg3958: Thence to the city, etc. The Scythopolitans, who by treating the Jews kindly earned from Judas thanks and praise for their kindnesses, signify those who receive holy teachers and confessors of the right faith, and help them with bodily comforts according to their means; their reward will not perish in vain, especially since the Lord in the Gospel says of such to the apostles: “He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet, shall receive the reward of a prophet: and he that receiveth a just man in the name of a just man, shall receive the reward of a just man; and whosoever shall give to drink to one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, amen I say to you, he shall not lose his reward.” Whence John also, writing to Gaius in his epistle, says: “Dearly beloved, thou dost faithfully whatever thou dost for the brethren, and that for strangers, who have given testimony to thy charity in the sight of the church: whom thou shalt do well to bring forward on their way in a manner worthy of God. Because for his name they went out, taking nothing of the Gentiles. We therefore ought to receive such, that we may be fellow helpers of the truth.” So also Paul praised such, writing to the Corinthians: “I beseech you, brethren, you know the house of Stephanas and of Fortunatus, that they are the firstfruits of Achaia, and have devoted themselves to the ministry of the saints, that you also be subject to such, and to every one that worketh with us and laboureth. And I rejoice in the patience of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus, because that which was wanting on your part, they have supplied. For they have refreshed both my spirit and yours. Know them therefore that are such.”
53_marg3959: And after Pentecost, etc. Gorgias, governor of Idumea, can well bear the type of the devil, who, always delighted in a red and bloody way of life, nevertheless sometimes feigns the appearance of virtues, although he himself by vices eagerly fights against the virtues. Whence he deceives and kills with craft any simple ones of the number of the faithful, yet does not obtain a lasting victory; rather, under the leadership of the true Judas, with his soldiers calling on the Lord as helper and persevering in prayers and hymns, the adverse party, confounded by fear, is turned to flight, and the honor of the whole triumph is given to the true worshippers of God. Whence Peter, writing to believers in his epistle, says: “Be you humbled therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in the time of visitation: casting all your care upon him, for he hath care of you. Be sober and watch: because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour: whom resist ye, strong in faith.” Hence also it is said through Paul: “Resist the devil, and he will fly from you.” As for Dositheus, who wished to take Gorgias alive but could not, because, his shoulder being cut off, the enemy escaped from his hands: this is by way of figure; it shows that the ancient enemy is conquered not by human strength but by divine aid. For he who, trusting in his own power with the Pelagians, hopes to be able to gain victory over the devil, not only does not conquer the enemy, but does not even keep the state of his own health unhurt.
53_marg3960: Those who were laid low by the enemy on account of hidden idolatry: whom could they signify better than those who defile themselves in the secret of the heart by covetousness and avarice? As though they carry under the tunic something from the offerings of idols, so are those who do works of virtue outwardly for the sake of earthly covetousness or the ambition of human praise, but beneath the veil of piety hide within the guile of wickedness. Such men are deservedly laid low by their enemies, because the poison of guile, which lay hidden from the sight of men, did not escape the gaze of the inner judge. That covetousness and avarice are idolatry, Paul shows, saying: “The desire of money is the root of all evils; which some coveting have erred from the faith, and have entangled themselves in many sorrows.” And again: “For know you this, he says, and understand, that no fornicator, or unclean, or covetous person (which is a serving of idols), hath inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.” For because of these things the wrath of God cometh upon the children of unbelief. Against this vice the Saviour, wishing to heal human minds, teaches in the Gospel, saying: “Take heed that you do not your justice before men, to be seen by them: otherwise you shall not have a reward of your Father who is in heaven.” And likewise: “Take heed, he says, and beware of all covetousness, for a man’s life doth not consist in the abundance of things which he possesseth.” The mystical Judas, considering that a fall has befallen his soldiers because of pretence, does not abandon them, but takes counsel with fatherly piety, both by interceding with prayers for their sins, and by correcting their error with the word of preaching and exhortation, so that, restored again to the worship of piety, they may thereafter watch themselves more carefully, lest by a like ruin they fall again into something worse, according to that of the Gospel: “Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest some worse thing happen to thee.”
53_marg3961: But the most valiant, etc. That after the departure from the present life prayer must be made for the sins of the faithful, and the work of almsgiving carried out, so that those for whose relief it is done may be loosed from sins, both the present passage shows, and the Lord in the Gospel, where, disputing about blasphemy against the Holy Spirit and showing that sin to be unforgivable, he says: “He that shall speak against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, nor in the world to come.” For in saying that this one sin is unforgivable, he shows that others can be forgiven both in the present and also in the future life. But how it is to be done for the salvation of the dead, the holy fathers show in their writings. Whence it has seemed good to insert in this work one chapter from the little works of holy Augustine, charging the reader to seek things like these in the sayings of other fathers. For the aforesaid father relates, in the work which he wrote to Laurentius on faith, hope and charity, speaking thus: The time which is placed between a man’s death and the final resurrection holds souls in hidden receptacles, as each is worthy, either of rest or of hardship, according to what it obtained in the flesh while it lived. Nor is it to be denied that the souls of the dead are relieved by the piety of their living kin, when the sacrifice of the Mediator is offered for them, or the almsgiving that is done in the Church; but these profit those who, while they lived, merited that these should afterwards profit them. For there is a certain way of living neither so good as not to need these things after death, nor so bad that these things do not profit after death. There is, then, one so good in his life that he does not need them, and again one so bad that he cannot be helped by them when this life has passed. Wherefore all merit is acquired here, by which anyone after this life may be relieved or burdened. Let no one think that what he has neglected here he will obtain from the Lord when he has died. Therefore these things which the Church practises in commending the dead are not contrary to that apostolic sentence which has been spoken: “For we must all be manifested before the judgment seat of Christ, that every one may receive the proper things of the body, according as he hath done, whether it be good or evil,” because each one acquired for himself, while he lived in the body, this merit, that these things might profit him. For they do not profit all; and why do they not profit all, if not because of the difference of life which each led in the body? When, therefore, sacrifices, whether of the altar or of alms of whatever amount, are offered for baptized dead, for the very good they are thanksgivings; for the not very bad they are propitiations; for the very bad, even if they are no help to the dead, they are some kind of consolations to the living; and for those whom they avail, they profit either that there may be full remission, or at least that damnation may be made more tolerable.
53_marg3962: But the king, with his mind. The history, which tells of the war of Antiochus Eupator and of Lysias his steward against the Jews, was recorded in the former book and at the same time explained according to the allegory. But that which is related next, that in the king’s camp by night fourteen thousand were slain by the Jews, and the greatest of the elephants with those who were set upon it, is more clearly expressed in the former narrative, where it is related that Eleazar the son of Saura, a Jew, seeing one of the beasts harnessed with the king’s harness, standing higher than the other beasts, since he thought that the king was on it, broke into the legion and ran under the feet of the elephant and slew it. And it, falling upon him, crushed him with its weight, and he died. Its spiritual signification was explained there, where the boasting of the proud is shown to be crushed by its own effort, as Scripture says: “Every arrogant man is an abomination before God.” And likewise: “Before destruction the heart is exalted, and before glory it is humbled.” And elsewhere: God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble. And in the Gospel the Lord says: “Every one that exalteth himself, shall be humbled: and he that humbleth himself, shall be exalted.” After this the history explains how Demetrius the son of Seleucus, coming into Judea and gaining the kingdom, was stirred up by Alcimus against Judas and his companions, where it is written thus: But Alcimus, etc.
53_marg3963: That it is said Alcimus offered to the king dice together with a golden crown and a palm, shows that by the judgment of his gifts he foretold and promised him the dignity of the kingdom and victory over his enemies, together with the worship of the temple. For they say the “talos” are offering vessels made in the manner of towers, with which they made offerings on the principal feasts; a likeness of them is still kept in some places. Now the Assideans are said to be those Jews who always laboured at divine worship, called from assiduity and named Assideans as though “assiduous”, such as Judas and his helpers were in the worship of God and the observance of his law. Others, however, assert that the Assideans were called from cleanness, as though “clean Jews”, because they separated themselves from idolatry and from the rite of the Gentiles. But Demetrius, having heard the report of Alcimus, whom the rest also, who were enemies of Judas, favoured in his accusation, forthwith sent Nicanor, the commander over the elephants, into Judea, with orders to take Judas himself, and “disperse all them that were with him, and to make Alcimus the high priest of the great temple.” Coming into Judea, he first pretended that he wished to have a covenant of peace with the Jews; afterwards, his enmity being made manifest, he showed himself a most wicked enemy rather than a faithful friend. But struck down by divine power, he paid the penalty of the blasphemy uttered against God and of his obstinacy; all of which is contained in the history of the former book, although some things which were omitted there because of the narrator’s haste are found inserted in the narration of this one. The allegorical sense, according to the measure of my poor wit, has been set out there on this same matter, and there is no need to repeat it now.
53_marg3964: Razias, a certain one, etc. Some, reading this and finding it written there that Razias, inflicting death on himself with his own hand, chose to die nobly rather than to become subject to sinners and to be treated with unworthy abuses against his noble birth, lest perhaps those of simpler mind believe that, when necessity presses, death is rather to be inflicted on themselves by some act of their own than that one should fall alive into the hands of sinners, I thought it would be useful to insert in this our work some things from the words of the venerable father Augustine, whence the sober reader may understand what he ought to do in such matters. Now the aforesaid father relates in his first book On the City of God, where he discussed in a copious treatise whether it is lawful for anyone to kill himself, speaking thus; for he says: Many have killed themselves lest they should come into the hands of their enemies. We do not now ask whether it was done, but whether it ought to have been done. Sound reason is to be put before even examples, and the examples do agree with it, but those which are the more worthy of imitation the more excellent they are in piety of soul. The patriarchs did not do it, nor the prophets, nor the apostles; for the Lord Christ himself, when he admonished them to flee from city to city if they suffered persecution, could have admonished them to lay hands on themselves, lest they come into the hands of their persecutors. Moreover, if he did not command or advise this, that they should depart from this life in that way, when he promised that for them as they departed he would prepare eternal mansions, whatever examples the Gentiles who know not God may offer, it is manifest that this is not lawful for those who worship the one true God. It remains that we understand of man what was said: “Thou shalt not kill,” neither another, nor yourself; for he who kills himself kills nothing other than a man. Yet the same divine authority has made certain exceptions, so that it is lawful for a man to be killed. But these are excepted, whom God commands to be killed, whether by a law given or by an express command for a particular person at a particular time. But he does not himself kill who owes his service to the one commanding, as a sword is an aid to him who uses it; and therefore they did in no way act against this precept, “Thou shalt not kill,” who waged wars at God’s bidding, or, bearing the person of public authority, according to the divine laws, that is, the command of most just reason, punished the wicked with death. And Abraham was not only not blamed with the charge of cruelty, but was even praised with the name of piety, because he willed to kill his son, not wickedly, but obediently. And rightly it is asked whether it is to be held as by God’s command that Jephte killed his daughter, who met her father, since he knew he would be sacrificing to God what first met him as he returned victorious from battle. Nor is Samson excused otherwise, who crushed himself together with his enemies by the fall of the house, except that the Spirit, who was working miracles through him, had secretly commanded this. With these excepted, then, whom the law, just in general, or God himself, the fountain of justice, specially commands to be killed, whoever kills a man, whether himself or anyone else, is bound by the charge of homicide; and those who have done this to themselves are perhaps to be admired for greatness of soul, not to be praised for soundness of wisdom. Yet if you consult reason more diligently, it is not even rightly called greatness of soul when one kills himself because he is unable to endure whatever hardships or the sins of others. For the mind is rather found weak which cannot bear either the hard servitude of its own body or the foolish opinion of the crowd; and that soul is to be called greater which can endure a wretched life rather than flee it, and despise human judgment, especially that of the common people, which is for the most part wrapped in the gloom of error, for the sake of the light and purity of conscience.
53_marg3965: But if anyone asks whether this vision can be referred to some mystery, this, unless I am mistaken, can be perceived in it: that Onias the priest signified the priestly order, and Jeremias the prophet, whose name means “high one of the Lord,” expresses the Lord himself, the head of the prophets. Of whom Moses says: “The Lord will raise up a prophet for you from among your brethren; him you shall hear as me.” And Isaias: “Cease ye,” he says, “from the man whose breath is in his nostrils, for he is reputed high.” The priestly order, therefore, through the men who under the old testament duly performed the divine office in the temple of God, not only made intercession for the sins of the people, but also showed forth the future incarnation of our mediator, by whose aid the world was to be saved. Of whom the apostle John says in his epistle: “We have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the just: and he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for those of the whole world.” He therefore gave the golden sword to Juda, when he granted to the holy doctors the divine scripture, shining with the spiritual sense, for the protection of the whole Church and the defence of his people, that they might use heavenly armour against all enemies, and lay low the multitude of the enemies.
53_marg3966: So all with a common. The book of Esther tells that, Aman persuading, the Agagite, King Assuerus commanded all the Jews in his kingdom to be put to death, and for carrying out this slaughter the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is called Adar, was appointed, and their goods to be plundered. But by the will of the Lord the same sentence was turned upon those who would strike them, so that the said king, through Mardochai the Jew, after the former writings, new letters being sent, commanded that on the very day on which slaughter was prepared for them by their enemies, the Jews should kill those enemies and persecutors of theirs. This they also did on the thirteenth and fourteenth day of the same month; of which it is written thus in the same history: The thirteenth day of the month Adar was the one day of slaughter with all, and on the fourteenth day they left off; which they appointed to be solemn, that on it thereafter for all time they might have leisure for feasting, joy, and banquets. Whence it is now written that, Nicanor being slain, and the help of God manifestly shown, all the Jews by common counsel decreed to keep the thirteenth day of the month Adar, which in the Syriac tongue is called the day before Mardochai’s day, as solemn for all time; and so these two solemnities agreed with each other. This is the one that is read in Machabees, and that other in Esther, so that those held on the thirteenth day and on the fourteenth day of the month Adar are joined together alike.
